title: Associate Director of Career Mentoring
description:
Position Overview

The Associate Director of Career Mentoring leads the
university-wide implementation of Career Mentoring for All,
advancing Butler’s commitment to ensure every student benefits from
meaningful career mentoring throughout their undergraduate
experience. The positions builds and sustains a scalable mentoring
model that helps students develop career readiness, build
professional networks, connect academic and experiential learning
to their goals and prepare for life after Butler.

Working across colleges and divisions, the Associate Director leads
the network of Career Mentors and College-Based Career Mentor
Leads. The position ensures a consistent, high-quality student
experience while supporting appropriate college-level adaption and
building the capacity of those delivering career mentoring across
the University.

Responsibilities

Lead university-wide implementation of Career Mentoring for
All, establishing the framework, standards, milestones, and
practices necessary to provide students with meaningful career
mentoring throughout their Butler experience.
Lead, supervise, and develop the Career Mentor team,
establishing clear expectations and share practices, providing
coaching and professional development, monitoring performance and
capacity, and ensuring Career Mentors effectively support students
and the College-Based Career Mentor Leads in delivering the
university-wide model.
Lead and convene the University and Career Mentoring Council
and support College-Based Career Leads, establishing shared
expectations; providing tools, training and ongoing support,
facilitation collaboration and problem-solving while helping
colleges and mentors adapt the university model to their students,
disciplines, and professional pathways.
Design and continuously strengthen the student career mentoring
experience, ensuring mentoring helps students develop career
readiness, professional identity, networks, and confidence while
preparing them to successful transition from Butler to employment,
graduate/professional education, or other post-graduate career
opportunities.
Connect career mentoring to Butler’s broader student
experiences, collaborating with academic advising and experiential
learning opportunities so students can translate their experiences
into skills, professional materials, and career direction.
Develop and sustain a robust network of career mentors,
partnering with Alumni Relations, employers, and other internal and
external partners to recruit, prepare, engage, recognize, and
retain mentors who reflect the range of students interests and
career pathways.
Build and manage the infrastructure necessary to deliver Career
Mentoring for All at scale, including student and mentor
preparation, matching processes, technology, communication,
resources, and operational practices to support an effective and
consistent experience.
Assess the effectiveness and outcomes of Career Mentoring for
all, using quantitative and qualitative data to identify gaps,
improve the student and mentor experience, inform decision-making,
and demonstrate the initiative’s contribution to career readiness
and post-graduate success.
Build a university-wide culture of career mentoring, engaging
students, faculty, staff, alumni, employers, and other partners in
understanding the value of career mentoring and their role in
preparing students for meaningful lives and careers.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Higher Education, Student Affairs,
Counseling, Organizational Leadership, Business Administration,
Human Resources Management, or related field.
Three to five years of progressively responsible experience in
career development, student success, higher education, mentoring,
experiential learning, alumni engagement, workforce development, or
a related area, including experience leading significant programs
or initiatives.
Demonstrated experience supervising, coaching, and developing
staff and building effective teams.
Demonstrated ability to build relationships, facilitate
collaboration, and influence across organizational boundaries and
among stakeholders with differing roles and perspectives.
Strong program and project management skills, including the
ability to translate strategic goals into sustainable practices and
manage multiple priorities.
Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and interpersonal
communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to use data and feedback to assess
effectiveness, identify opportunities, and improve programs and
experiences.
Commitment to creating high-quality and equitable experiences
that support students with a wide range of backgrounds, interests,
and career pathways.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree preferred
Experience managing mentoring, volunteer, alumni engagement, or
student success programs.
Experience administering mentoring software, CRM systems, or
student engagement platforms.
Knowledge of career development, student success, retention,
and workforce readiness practices.
Experience recruiting, training, and managing
volunteers.

About Us

Butler University is a private, nationally recognized comprehensive
university encompassing seven colleges: Arts, Business,
Communication, Education, Liberal Arts & Sciences, Pharmacy
& Health Sciences and Founder's College. Approximately 4,500
undergraduate and 1,000 graduate and doctoral students are enrolled
at Butler, representing 46 states and 24 countries.

Join us at the crossroads of tradition & transformation. A
career at Butler University offers more than just a job—it’s an
opportunity to join a dedicated, innovative, and supportive
community grounded in equity, academic excellence, and meaningful
impact. Aligned with Boldly Butler, our strategic plan, faculty and
staff play a vital role in delivering transformational learning
experiences, enriching our campus and community, and ensuring a
thriving Butler for generations to come.

Butler University is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome
applications from all individuals, regardless of age, sex, race,
religion, color, disability, protected veteran status, national
origin, or any other legally protected category.
